mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the real discount rate applied to future equity valuations, thereby depressing the present value of expected future cash flows and pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the same regime are not statistically lower than the pre-rate hike period (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS decline occurs without a corresponding SPX drop.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 3% for the first time in a 6-month window, the market anticipates a pre-emptive rate hike, causing a short-term spike in risk-free rates and a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% over a 6-month window
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns do not turn negative within 3 days of the inflation crossing, or the S&P 500 outperforms the risk-free rate by at least 1% over the same horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in PAYEMS labor cost index (>10% month-over-month) combined with a simultaneous decline in UNRATE unemployment suggests tight labor markets, prompting equity valuation adjustments that produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases >10% MoM AND UNRATE decreases >0.2% MoM
failure_condition: No significant positive SPX 5-day returns in 10 consecutive such labor market events, or the correlation between PAYEMS/UNRATE change and SPX return falls below 0.3.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly GDPC1 personal consumption expenditure grows at a rate exceeding 6% from the prior quarter, the market infers robust consumer demand that supports higher corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Quarterly returns in >10 similar events do not beat a 2% risk-free benchmark, or SPX volatility spikes without a directional bias.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO manufacturing index for three months indicates weakening supply capacity, which the market interprets as a risk of softer earnings and a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns in such supply contraction regimes are not statistically worse than during neutral supply conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for four consecutive months, the market expects future rate cuts, lowering real discount rates and supporting higher equity valuations, which should produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns in this regime do not exceed the historical average for rate-cut anticipation periods.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months while HOUST (household spending) rises by at least 4% month-over-month, it signals a strengthening labor market and consumer confidence, which should drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% for two consecutive months AND HOUST increases >4% MoM
regime_hint: labor market strengthening coupled with consumer spending acceleration
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive SPX returns within 10 such labor+spending events, or the interaction p-value exceeds 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In regimes where both RSAFS (demand) and UNRATE (labor) show simultaneous improvement (RSAFS up >2% and UNRATE down <1% over the prior month), the market anticipates a dual-stimulus environment that consistently yields positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases >2% AND UNRATE decreases <1% over the prior month
regime_hint: simultaneous demand and labor market improvement
failure_condition: Across 15 such dual-improvement events, the 20-day forward return mean is not statistically higher than zero (p > 0.05).
